title: Device-independent Quantum Key Distribution in the commuting operator framework
authors: Gereon Koßmann, René Schwonnek, Po-Chieh Liu, Hao-Chung Cheng
abstract: Device-independent quantum key distribution (DIQKD) is arguably the gold standard for secure quantum communication, as it aims to rely only on observed input-output statistics of an uncharacterized device which is only assumption to obey the laws of quantum physics. A corresponding security analysis hence demands a description of a quantum experiment from a most general perspective. Under close inspection, existing proof techniques do not always meet this goal as they tend to rely on subtile assumptions on a tensor product structure of the underlying Hilbert space and a 'hidden but finite' dimensionality. In this work, we collect the tools needed for a full analysis of DIQKD in the commuting operator framework, which avoids these subtilities and provides the arguably most general view on a quantum experiment. We rigorously proof the common assumption that in DIQKD measurements can be w.l.o.g. assumed to be projective. Furthermore, we show that task of computing key rates can be casted as a non-commutative polynomial optimization (NPO) problem to which the Navascués-Pironio-Acín (NPA) hierarchy gives a correct and converging relaxation.   As a tool, we generalize the integral representation for the relative entropy by Frenkel [Quantum 7, 1102 (2023)] to general von Neumann algebras and apply techniques from Kossmann and Schwonnek [arXiv: 2411.04858] for the approximation in an NPO program.
summary: This paper advances the theoretical understanding of Device-Independent Quantum Key Distribution by reformulating security analysis within the general commuting-operator framework. It overcomes limitations of previous methods that required restrictive structural assumptions on the underlying Hilbert space. The work establishes a rigorous mathematical link between observed quantum statistics and achievable key rates via non-commutative polynomial optimization.
main_problem: To develop a maximally general mathematical framework for analyzing Device-Independent Quantum Key Distribution (DIQKD) security that avoids restrictive assumptions found in existing proof techniques.
main_result: The authors provide a representation-independent route from observed statistics to an AEP-based security statement using the commuting operator framework, and show key rate computation maps to a solvable Non-Commutative Polynomial Optimization (NPO) problem.
method: The work employs advanced tools from von Neumann algebras, generalizing relative entropy calculations (Frenkel's formula) and casting the optimization problem into an NPA hierarchy relaxation scheme.
model_or_system: The study models DIQKD experiments using the commuting-operator framework, which utilizes universal C*-algebras to represent local operations for Alice and Bob, thereby avoiding assumptions about tensor product structures in the Hilbert space.
key_observables: Secure key rates, relative entropy, and conditional von Neumann entropy.
important_parameters: The security analysis depends on observed input-output statistics of the uncharacterized device.
main_assumptions: The framework aims to overcome assumptions regarding tensor product structure and hidden finite dimensionality inherent in prior DIQKD analyses.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the general setup of a DIQKD experiment involving Alice, Bob, a source, and local random number generators.
paper_structure: The paper builds by first establishing the commuting-operator framework, then generalizing necessary tools like relative entropy to von Neumann algebras, proving key technical results (like PVM assumption), and finally formulating the security rate calculation as an NPO problem solvable via NPA relaxations.
why_interesting: While focused on quantum cryptography, the reliance on advanced operator algebra techniques (von Neumann algebras) and optimization theory provides deep mathematical tools applicable to analyzing open quantum systems where standard Hilbert space assumptions break down.

figures.caption: Figure 1. The figure illustrates a device-independent quantum key distribution (DIQKD) experiment. In contrast to the quantum game depicted in Figure 2, the referee is replaced by local random number generators (RNGs), one on each side. While sharing a quantum state ρAB, Alice and Bob use their respective RNGs to draw private and local random inputs, feed them into their devices, and collect the resulting output statistics.

Figure 2. The figure illustrates a non-local quantum game. A source prepares a bipartite state ρAB and distributes it between Alice and Bob. Following a predetermined strategy, specified by the shared state together with their local measurements, Alice and Bob receive questions x ∈X and y ∈Y from a referee, feed them as inputs into their respective devices, and respond with the outcomes a ∈A and b ∈B produced by their local boxes.
